ratings.reason: Uses S4 as the DHODH-differentiation core and S1/S2/S3 for context/comparator while explicitly marking teriflunomide approval, DHODH potency, free Cmax, uridine rescue and marrow exposure as unverified. The design has numeric gates, viability-matched cell-cycle control, uridine rescue and normal-CD34 selectivity, but no packet source directly validates the drug or its AML exposure.

ratings.reason: Mechanistic ordering, ATP-intact timing, URA1 epistasis and enzyme selectivity are strong, and the text flags atovaquone indication, protein binding, complex III potency, ubiquinone-DHODH and URA1 as unverified. Grounding is low because S2/S4 do not link atovaquone, complex III, ubiquinone or salvage limitation to AML; many gates also strain feasibility.

Endpoints and falsifiers are testable; specificity is lower because the design uses one PDX and no numeric free-drug or salvage threshold.

ratings.reason: The design separates pyrimidine depletion from ATP collapse with ubiquinone, uridine and respiratory-independent DHODH rescue. ratings.novelty_note: The distinctive novelty is an operational salvage-flux/demand ratio R=C/D with bidirectional salvage perturbation as the sensitivity determinant; it overlaps P37c0129eed and prior teriflunomide/leflunomide or salvage-resistance AML literature must be searched.
ratings.reason: This is the most causally explicit design: it predefines exposure envelope, isotope-based salvage/demand, lineage tracking, uridine rescue and reciprocal genetic perturbation. S4/S2 support pathway and residual context only, while teriflunomide, UCK/transport, human exposure and normal-progenitor compensation remain unverified; the complexity reduces feasibility.

ratings.reason: It integrates S4 target rationale, S1-S3 context/comparator, clear engagement/rescue/genetic and normal-CD34 selectivity tests, with staged combination only after single-agent validation. Central drug approval, exposure, DHODH dependence and salvage assumptions remain unverified, and feasibility is moderate because of panel size and PDX work.

ratings.reason: Anchors DHODH differentiation to S4 and residual oxidative biology to S2, while explicitly separating ROS-low LSC and the venetoclax-azacitidine comparator. Causal dissection using R=C/D, isotope-confirmed rescue, lineage tracking, and bidirectional salvage perturbation is strong; feasibility is reduced by demanding absolute flux/demand measurements and secondary transplantation.

ratings.reason: Packet support for oxidative residual cells (S2) and DHODH differentiation (S4) is used appropriately, but atovaquone's mammalian complex III inhibition, ubiquinone coupling, and free exposure are unverified. Epistasis with uridine and a respiratory-chain-independent DHODH construct plus enzyme assays gives good causal discrimination, though exposure and normal-progenitor selectivity remain major feasibility risks.

ratings.reason: Uses S4 as the central DHODH-differentiation premise and correctly separates S1, S2, and S3 contexts, with unverified approval, target, and exposure facts labeled. The validation plan has target engagement, uridine rescue, maturation-before-viability ordering, and normal CD34 selectivity, but is less quantitatively gated and less causally dissected than the strongest proposals.

ratings.novelty_note: Low-uridine-salvage teriflunomide repurposing in cytarabine-residual AML; nearly the same core concept as Pf3e8bf3aee, so novelty is not established and prior salvage/DHODH-AML literature must be checked.
ratings.reason: Grounds the DHODH-differentiation rationale in S4 and residual oxidative context in S2, while explicitly preserving S1 LSC and S3 comparator boundaries. Labeled-uridine salvage, pyrimidine rescue, genotype-confirmed maturation, and secondary transplantation provide good causal discrimination and falsification, but the experiments are technically demanding.

ratings.novelty_note: Atovaquone repurposing with a salvage-gated, ubiquinone-timed DHODH mechanism in cytarabine-residual AML; highly specified, but the drug-specific mechanism is outside the packet and prior atovaquone AML studies could constrain novelty.
ratings.reason: The packet directly supports only S2 oxidative residual biology and S4 DHODH differentiation, not atovaquone's complex III/ubiquinone/DHODH linkage or free exposure. The proposal nevertheless provides exceptional causal rigor with prespecified eligibility gates, temporal ATP-intact ordering, uridine/URA1 rescue, enzyme specificity, and clear go/no-go falsifiers, at the cost of high experimental complexity.

ratings.novelty_note: Teriflunomide DHODH-directed differentiation in gated immature AML, separated from venetoclax-azacitidine oxidative-phosphorylation effects; novelty overlaps with other teriflunomide proposals and is unproven without prior-literature checking.
ratings.reason: Strongly anchored to S4's DHODH-differentiation result and S1/S3/S2 context separation, with drug approval, target, and exposure labeled unverified. Same-sample pathway suppression, uridine rescue, viability-matched cell-cycle controls, brequinar and venetoclax-azacitidine comparators, and numeric selectivity/falsification thresholds make it specific and testable with feasible in vitro primary-cell work.
